item.title: PICKLES: Covariance-Preconditioned Kinetic Langevin Ensemble Sampler
item.description: arXiv:2610.24295v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a covariance-preconditioned kinetic Langevin ensemble sampler named PICKLES. This is a kinetic analogue of the affine invariant interacting Langevin dynamics (ALDI). PICKLES uses a rectangular covariance square root as a preconditioner to avoid computing matrix inverses or square roots, leading to position and momentum variables of different dimensions. Theoretically, the continuous-time dynamics are ergodic under mild regularity and growth conditions on the potential, assuming $N>d+1$ particles and a full-rank initial ensemble. We discretize PICKLES using BAOAB or OBABO splitting, with the latter convenient for Metropolization. For Gaussian targets at stationarity, we demonstrate that Metropolized PICKLES achieves an integration step size scaling of $d^{-1/4}$ to achieve fixed acceptance probabilities, as the ensemble size and dimension increase at a fixed ratio. This matches the scaling of single particle Metropolized Hamiltonian and kinetic samplers. Numerical experiments compare sampling efficiency and estimation error with non-preconditioned, overdamped, and single-chain counterparts, demonstrating improved efficiency per gradient evaluation. On a Dark Energy Survey Year 1 3x2pt cosmology benchmark, we obtain competitive effective sample size per gradient evaluation compared to a densely preconditioned No-U-Turn Sampler.
item.dc:creator: Hong Ye Tan, Stanley Osher, Yifan Chen

item.title: Exploiting sparse conditional dependence in remote sensing observing systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.24710v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a novel filtering algorithm for remote sensing inverse problems that exploits sparsity in the precision (inverse covariance) matrix arising from conditional independence structures in spatio-temporal satellite data. Motivated by NASA's Orbiting Carbon Observatory-2 (OCO-2), Earth Surface Mineral Dust Source Investigation (EMIT), and upcoming Explorer for Artemis Geology Lunar and Earth (EAGLE) missions, we formulate a Bayesian inference framework for retrieving atmospheric and surface parameters from hyperspectral radiance measurements. Unlike traditional methods that operate on covariances and ignore spatio-temporal dependencies, our approach models the full spatio-temporal state using sparse Gaussian graphical models, which corresponds to a block-sparse precision matrix. We derive an information filter based on this structure, enabling scalable joint inference over large spatial grids with uncertainty propagation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the algorithm in two distinct remote sensing contexts. First, we apply the method to synthetic data configured to mimic the OCO-2 mission, focusing on retrievals of atmospheric CO$_2$, and observe a 50% reduction in CO$_2$ retrieval error compared to single-pixel methods. Then, we evaluate the algorithm using imaging spectroscopy data from the Surface Biology and Geology (SBG) High Frequency Time Series (SHIFT) campaign to retrieve surface reflectance, achieving a 20% reduction in retrieval error relative to baseline approaches.
item.dc:creator: Kelvin M. Leung, Jouni Susiluoto, Regina Eckert, Youssef Marzouk

item.title: lepidoptera: A Domain-Agnostic Engine for Causal Simulation with Mixed Variable Types, Vine Copula Dependence, and Individual-Level Counterfactual Propagation
item.description: arXiv:2610.24147v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: lepidoptera is an open-source R and Python package for simulation from structural causal models with heterogeneous variable types. The package is built around a typed mechanism architecture, which separates the causal graph from the generating rule at each node and exposes each rule as an inspectable, serialisable object. A pre-built mechanism library covers all nine combinations of continuous, categorical, and ordinal parent and child types, removing the need for users to implement type-specific sampling from scratch. A vine copula mechanism estimates the full joint dependence structure from observed data using pair-copula constructions and the Rosenblatt conditional-simulation algorithm, supporting over twenty copula families. Individual-level counterfactual queries are supported through partial propagation, which freezes the random draws of unaffected nodes and replays only the downstream consequences of an intervention, thereby separating the individual treatment effect (ITE) estimand from the population-level average treatment effect (ATE) without additional model assumptions. An extension layer allows any pre-fitted predictive model to serve as a generative mechanism via a unified callable interface. Three worked illustrations spanning clinical trial planning, emergency-ward capacity analysis, and epidemiological mediation analysis demonstrate the package's scope.
item.dc:creator: Danilo Augusto Sarti

item.title: Censored Flow Matching for Synthetic Time-to-Event Generation
item.description: arXiv:2610.24233v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generating time-to-event data is increasingly important in survival analysis, but it remains statistically challenging because event times are often censored and thus prevent flexible generative modeling. To fill this gap, we propose a novel method called censored flow matching (CFM), aiming at providing a flexible flow-based generative mechanism for synthesizing time-to-event data as well as learning their corresponding probabilistic densities. Unlike existing methods, CFM does not rely on survival likelihoods to handle censoring, but instead exploits the monotonicity property of differential flows to address censoring via pullback sampling. Under this framework, we implement an alternating procedure between pullback sampling and CFM steps, leading to a flow-based expectation--maximization (EM) algorithm tailored for time-to-event inference. Under mild distributional conditions, we establish the convergence of CFM to the true event-time distribution as the EM iterations proceed. We then apply CFM to generate time-to-event data and estimate their probabilistic densities, where the observed censoring time can be incorporated to provide truncated sampling or truncated density estimation for survival inference. Through extensive simulation studies, we demonstrate the benefits of CFM for complex and large-scale data generation. Finally, we apply CFM to analyze data from the Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network (OPTN) and the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV), showcasing its benefits for synthetic and predictive survival analyses in terms of data fidelity, predictive performance, and empirical privacy characteristics.
item.dc:creator: Jianbin Tan, Xingran Chen, Kevin He, Zhenke Wu, Bhramar Mukherjee, Anru R. Zhang

item.title: Federated Community Detection in Bipartite Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.25997v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study federated spectral estimation when a large matrix is horizontally partitioned across servers that cannot share raw data. We propose FLICKER, a target-specific gradient-based power iteration that recovers a singular direction associated with a prescribed spectral target using only matrix-vector products on local blocks. Different target directions can be recovered independently and in parallel. We establish non-asymptotic convergence guarantees and provide a recursive grid-search procedure for spectral target selection. Building on FLICKER, we develop BiFLICKER for federated community detection in bipartite networks, together with a sequential projected variant for nearby or repeated singular directions. Under a sparse bipartite stochastic block model, we show that properly rescaled leading singular values from a reference server provide valid global targets, and that Sequential BiFLICKER achieves a vanishing misclustering rate and exact recovery under stronger sparsity conditions. Simulations show that BiFLICKER remains close to centralized spectral clustering and is more robust than existing federated spectral baselines when local sample sizes are small. On a LastFM user-artist network naturally partitioned by country, Sequential BiFLICKER attains an overall ARI of 0.94 against centralized clustering while revealing cross-country communities with distinct listening profiles.
item.dc:creator: Wanjie Wang

item.title: Interacting Annealed Importance Sampling via Population-Based MCMC Kernels
item.description: arXiv:2401.15645v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Sampling from a multimodal distribution is a fundamental and challenging problem in computational science and statistics. Among various approaches proposed for this task, one popular method is Annealed Importance Sampling (AIS). In this paper, we propose an interaction-based version of AIS by combining it with population-based Monte Carlo methods to improve its efficiency. By keeping track of an ensemble instead of a single sampler along some continuation path between the starting distribution and the target distribution, we take advantage of the interaction within the ensemble to encourage the exploration of undiscovered modes. Specifically, our main idea is to utilize either the snooker algorithm or the genetic algorithm used in Evolutionary Monte Carlo. We discuss how the proposed algorithm can be implemented and derive a partial differential equation governing the evolution of the ensemble under the continuous time and mean-field limit. We also test the efficiency of the proposed algorithm on various continuous and discrete distributions.
item.dc:creator: Haoxuan Chen, Lexing Ying

item.title: Ensemble Control Variates
item.description: arXiv:2509.01091v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Control variates have become an increasingly popular variance-reduction technique in Bayesian inference. Many broadly applicable control variates are based on the Langevin-Stein operator, which leverages gradient information available from gradient-based samplers to produce variance-reduced estimators of expectations. These control variates typically require optimising over a function $u(\theta)$ within a user-defined functional class $\mathcal{G}$, such as the space of $Q$th-order polynomials or a reproducing kernel Hilbert space. We propose using averaging-based ensemble learning to construct Stein-based control variates. While the proposed framework is broadly applicable, we focus on ensembles constructed from zero-variance control variates (ZVCV), a popular parametric approach based on solving a linear approximation problem that can easily be over-parameterised in medium-to-high dimensional settings. A common remedy is to use regularised ZVCV via penalised regression, but these methods can be prohibitively slow. We introduce ensemble ZVCV methods based on ensembles of OLS estimators and evaluate the proposed methods against established methods in the literature in a simulation study. Our results show that ensemble ZVCV methods are more statistically efficient than regularised ZVCV methods, while also being substantially faster. This work opens a new direction for constructing broadly applicable control variate techniques via ensemble learning.
item.dc:creator: Minh-Long Nguyen, Christopher Drovandi, Leah F. South

item.title: Scalable Bayesian Clustering for Integrative Analysis of Multi-View Data
item.description: arXiv:2408.17153v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In the era of Big Data, scalable and accurate clustering algorithms for high-dimensional data are essential. We present new Bayesian Distance Clustering (BDC) models and inference algorithms with improved scalability while maintaining the predictive accuracy of modern Bayesian nonparametric models. Unlike traditional methods, BDC models the distance between observations rather than the observations directly, offering a compromise between the scalability of distance-based methods and the enhanced predictive power and probabilistic interpretation of model-based methods. However, existing BDC models still rely on performing inference on the partition model to group observations into clusters. The support of this partition model grows exponentially with the dataset's size, complicating posterior space exploration and leading to many costly likelihood evaluations. Inspired by $k$-medoids, we propose using tessellations in discrete space to simplify inference by focusing the learning task on finding the best tessellation centers, or "medoids". Additionally, we extend our models to effectively handle multi-view data, such as data comprised of clusters that evolve across time, enhancing their applicability to complex datasets. The real data application in numismatics demonstrates the efficacy of our approach.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Gianella, Rafael Cabral, Andrew Harris, Maria De Iorio

item.title: A Stable Lasso
item.description: arXiv:2511.02306v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Lasso has been widely used as a method for variable selection, valued for its simplicity and empirical performance. However, Lasso's selection stability deteriorates in the presence of correlated predictors. Several approaches have been developed to mitigate this limitation. In this paper, we provide a brief review of existing approaches, highlighting their limitations. We then propose a technique to improve the selection stability of Lasso by integrating a weighting scheme into the Lasso penalty function, where the weights are defined as an increasing function of a correlation-adjusted ranking that reflects the predictive power of predictors. Empirical evaluations on both simulated and real-world datasets demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed method. Additional numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in stabilizing other regularization-based selection methods, indicating its potential as a general-purpose solution.
item.dc:creator: Mahdi Nouraie, Houying Zhu, Samuel Muller

item.title: Ergodic Central limit theorem for subgeometric Markov chains
item.description: arXiv:2512.18255v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish verifiable necessary conditions for central limit theorems (CLTs) of ergodic averages of Markov chains on general state spaces. Our criteria are based on discrete-time $\mathbf{L}$-drift conditions that can be verified through estimates for the one-step transition kernel of the original chain. They yield an integral criterion for failure of the CLT for a class of observables that includes unbounded functions and indicators of tail events. The main technical step transfers lower bounds for excursions of the original chain to regenerative excursions of its Nummelin split chain. The same drift conditions yield lower bounds on the tails of return times and modulated excursion functionals, on invariant tails, and on rates of convergence in $f$-variation and $L^p$-Wasserstein distance. These estimates apply without an explicit formula for the invariant distribution. Applications to unadjusted Langevin algorithms show preservation of polynomial target tail indices at every fixed step size. For Euler schemes with additive infinite-variance noise, we establish restrictions on invariant tails and transience under superlinear drifts. Schemes with linear drift, multiplicative noise and logarithmic innovation tails exhibit sharp polynomial convergence exponents and exact CLT thresholds, despite the absence of positive Euclidean moments.
item.dc:creator: Miha Bre\v{s}ar, Aleksandar Mijatovi\'c, Gareth Roberts

item.title: Relaxation times of non-reversible Markov processes
item.description: arXiv:2607.10801v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a systematic approach to quantify $L^2$-relaxation times for non-reversible Markov processes based on the singular value gap of the generator introduced by Chatterjee. The inverse of the singular value gap is equivalent to the relaxation time of the time-averaged transition semigroup. We show that, moreover, the inverse singular value gap of the two-point motion is equivalent to the relaxation time of the non-averaged transition semigroup, and that it provides a lower bound on the usual spectral gap of the generator. We then introduce a method for deriving lower bounds on singular value gaps for Markov processes with degenerate noise that is based on the concept of a first- and second-order collapse of the generator. It follows ideas from hypocoercivity developed in a previous series of works but is simpler and more broadly applicable. In contrast to previous results, it includes settings with non-vanishing first-order collapse, and thus applies directly to Markov chains (in continuous time), but also to diffusion processes and piecewise-deterministic Markov processes. Our approach yields sharp upper and lower bounds for several classes of examples. First applications include the proof of a conjecture by Diaconis and Miclo on a square-root speed-up for lifted random walks on abelian groups, as well as bounds on relaxation times of switching flows perturbed by noise and of non-reversible diffusion processes.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Eberle, Francis L\"orler
